title: Etude comparative de la morphologie de l'oeil chez quatre espèces de lézards tropicaux (Scincidae) occupant différentes niches écologiques
why: Sphenomorphus: a 2024 poster from the Université de Mons comparing eye morphology in four tropical skink species that occupy different ecological niches. The harvest stores no abstract ("editorial reviewed"), so the four species are not visible. It came back in the Scincidae family review of the harvest and for the web searches "forest skink visual acuity", "forest skink visual field" and "forest skink pupil shape", with its abstract PDF (bitstream 51244/2). A Sphenomorphus species could be among the four, since the genus is tropical, and eye morphology can give eye and lens dimensions that bear on acuity_cpd, whether the retina has a fovea (fovea) and a pupil shape (pupil_shape). Main's harvest-37 put the same poster on the wanted list for Trachylepis. The author is the name the file name shows. Not opened. Re-pointed after audit 62, which opened the abstract (ORBi bitstream 51244/2): the four skinks are Tribolonotus gracilis, Mochlus fernandi, Tiliqua gigas and T. scincoides, with no Sphenomorphus, so the poster can fill no Sphenomorphus cell. It bears on the Tiliqua scincoides pupil_shape and fovea cells, open at species level (its acuity_cpd is filled at genus level from T. rugosa), and through M. fernandi on the open cells of Mochlus sundevallii. The abstract lists four authors (Gennaux, Dolinskii, Boutry and Nonclercq) and prints no year or meeting; the year is the file name's.

title: The visual cliff
why: Capra depth_cue: the web search "visual cliff goat kids depth perception Gibson Walk" (run after "Capra depth perception" and "goat depth perception" returned only general and popular pages) returned the Wikipedia article on the visual cliff and secondary accounts headed "Visual Cliff Experiment (Gibson & Walk, 1960)" and "Gibson & Walk (1960): The Visual Cliff" (Simply Psychology, Cognito, flashcard sites). The visual-cliff test shows whether a young animal avoids an apparent drop, a behavioural measure of depth perception; that goat kids were among the young animals tested is my own recollection, and none of the returned titles shows it. If they were, the article gives a depth_cue row for Capra hircus (depth perception shown behaviourally, cue unnamed). The journal, volume and pages are not given here because no result showed them. Main holds no depth_cue row for a goat; its one bovid row is the sheep (canon-3#4, Nityananda and Read 2017), and the harvest's citation step on that review found 0 works naming Capra. Not opened. Audit 62 opened the Wikipedia article on the visual cliff, which gives the article as Scientific American 202(4): 64-71 (April 1960) and lists newborn kids among the animals tested, so the 1960 article should give a behavioural depth_cue row for Capra hircus.
get: journal via library (the 1960 article); secondary accounts: https://www.simplypsychology.org/visual-cliff-experiment.html

title: An Overview of the Penguin Visual System
why: Spheniscus acuity_cpd and interreceptor_deg: a review of the penguin visual system, the top result of the web search "Magellanic penguin visual acuity" (its PubMed Central, MDPI and DOAJ copies and an Encyclopedia entry also came back, and the MDPI copy for "Spheniscus visual acuity") and a hit of the harvest query "Spheniscus visual acuity". Main's sweep-53 opened it and reports that it gives cone-pigment and photoreceptor-spacing figures for the Humboldt, king and Magellanic penguins; main has logged from it only the Humboldt penguin's spectral range (sweep-48) and a gentoo acuity (sweep-57), and sweep-48 recorded Spheniscus acuity and receptor spacing as not found. The photoreceptor spacing of Spheniscus humboldti and S. magellanicus (interreceptor_deg, through the eye's nodal distance) and any acuity it reports for a banded penguin (acuity_cpd) should be logged with their primary sources. A search for the primary retina work ("Magellanic penguin retina photoreceptor cone density Spheniscus magellanicus") returned an Argentine CONICET repository record (https://ri.conicet.gov.ar/handle/11336/96381), a Chilean ANID researcher record (work 82750), a SciCrunch record (20737597) and an EPA HERO reference (7628642), all shown without titles, and the 1985 pigment and oil-droplet study of S. humboldti (10.1007/BF00610668); the CONICET record may be that primary work. Not opened by this desk. Authors from the Crossref record (desk Crossref run 30, 18 October 2026). Audit 62 read the review: its photoreceptor-spacing figure is the king penguin's, and for the Magellanic penguin it gives a cone-to-rod ratio and maximum ganglion-cell densities of 7,800 to 12,000 cells (per square millimetre by the auditor's reading) from its reference 94, so the review itself holds no Spheniscus spacing or acuity. Coimbra, Nolan, Collin and Hart 2012 on the ganglion-cell topography and spatial resolving power of penguins (10.1159/000341901, wanted as audit-62) is the primary work to read for these cells.
